newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite lawyer.

text.p: Two gunmen killed a Shi'ite Moslem lawyer in Pakistan's central province of Punjab on Saturday amid heightened tension between militant groups of the rival Islamic Sunni and Shi'ite sects, police said.

They said Jarrar Zaidi, president of a Shi'ite centre in his home town of Sheikhpura and a two-time former president of the local bar association, was shot by the unknown men as he waited for a taxi near his home to go to Sheikhupura courts, 40 km (25 miles) from the provincial capital Lahore.
The gunmen, who were riding a motorcyle, shot Zaidi in the head and neck, police said. He later died being shifted to a hospital in Lahore.

Tension between the militant groups of the majority Sunnis and the minority Shi'ites has heightened after suspected Sunni militants burst into an Iranian cultural centre in Punjab's Multan city on Thursday and killed eight people, including its Iranian director Muhammad Ali Rahimi.

Police said on Friday they had arrested two Sunni militants suspected of attacking the Iranian centre and seized 13 rocket-launchers, three assault rifles, five hand grenades and other weapons and ammunition from them.

Differences over the interpretation of Islamic beliefs have often flared into violence between Sunnis, who dominate Pakistan's population of more than 130 million, and Shi'ites, who constitute about 15 percent.
